title: xHCI spec -- Host Controller operational register map (USBCMD/USBSTS/CRCR/DCBAAP/PORTSC) and the full TRB Type enumeration with ring-legality rules
summary: Deep extraction of D:\DV\Task\USB\DOC\extensible-host-controler-interface-usb-xhci.pdf, citations in .work\pdftxt\xhci.txt (31654 lines). This is the Host Controller register-level programming interface spec -- different in kind from the 3 link-protocol specs (usb_20/usb32/UTMI+): defines the SW/HW register map, ring-based command/transfer data structures (TRBs), and slot/endpoint context model a Host Controller and its driver implement. Directly relevant for modeling/verifying a USB3 host controller DUT or host-side VIP/BFM. OPERATIONAL REGISTER MAP (Table 5-18, sec 5.4, p.391, lines 19091-19156): 00h=USBCMD(USB Command,5.4.1), 04h=USBSTS(USB Status,5.4.2), 08h=PAGESIZE(5.4.3), 0C-13h=RsvdZ, 14h=DNCTRL(Device Notification Control,5.4.4), 18h=CRCR(Command Ring Control,5.4.5), 20-2Fh=RsvdZ, 30h=DCBAAP(Device Context Base Address Array Pointer,5.4.6), 38h=CONFIG(Configure,5.4.7), 3C-3FFh=RsvdZ, 400-13FFh=Port Register Set 1..MaxPorts (grouped consecutive Dwords per port: PORTSC offset0h/PORTPMSC offset4h/PORTLI offset8h/PORTHLPMC offsetCh -- Table 5-19, lines 19137-19148; MaxPorts comes from the HCSPARAMS1 capability register). Virtualization note: when Operational Registers are exposed via a Virtual Function (VF) they are emulated by the VMM with discretion over write effects/read values -- relevant only if SR-IOV/VF modeling is ever needed. USBCMD (sec 5.4.1, lines 19157-19180+): 32-bit RO/RW mixed, default 0; bit0=Run/Stop(R/S) -- 1=Run(xHC executes schedule as long as bit stays 1), 0=Stop. Other named bits visible in the Figure 5-14 bitfield diagram but not individually decoded this pass: INTE, HSEE, LHCRST, CSS, CRS, EWE, EU3S, CME, ETE, TSCEN, VTIOEN (flagged for a future deeper pass rather than guessed). TRB STRUCTURE (sec 4.11, p.208-209, lines 10062-10151): 3 components per TRB -- Parameter, Status, Control (each 32-bit Dword, 3 Dwords total... actually 4 Dwords/16 bytes per TRB with TRB Type always in Control bits10-15 and Cycle bit always in Control bit0). Producer/consumer roles differ by ring: Command/Transfer rings = system software produces, xHC consumes (all fields read-only to xHC once written); Event ring = xHC produces, system software consumes. Ordering constraint for a BFM: if a TRB's 4 Dwords aren't written atomically, Parameter+Status must be initialized BEFORE writing Control (since Control carries the Cycle bit that makes the TRB visible to the xHC) -- writing Control must happen last. Bus-mastering note: xHC architected around >=16-byte atomic TRB reads (larger bursts, e.g. 4 TRBs in one 64B transaction, allowed for efficiency). TRB TYPE ENUMERATION (Table 6-91, p.511-512, lines 25248-25340) -- full ID list with ring-legality: 0=Reserved; 1=Normal(Transfer); 2=Setup Stage(Transfer); 3=Data Stage(Transfer); 4=Status Stage(Transfer); 5=Isoch(Transfer); 6=Link(Command+Transfer); 7=Event Data(Command+Transfer); 8=No-Op(Command+Transfer); 9=Enable Slot Command; 10=Disable Slot Command; 11=Address Device Command; 12=Configure Endpoint Command; 13=Evaluate Context Command; 14=Reset Endpoint Command; 15=Stop Endpoint Command; 16=Set TR Dequeue Pointer Command; 17=Reset Device Command; 18=Force Event Command(optional,virtualization only); 19=Negotiate Bandwidth Command(optional); 20=Set Latency Tolerance Value Command(optional); 21=Get Port Bandwidth Command(optional); 22=Force Header Command; 23=No Op Command; 24=Get Extended Property Command(optional); 25=Set Extended Property Command(optional); 26-31=Reserved; 32=Transfer Event; 33=Command Completion Event; 34=Port Status Change Event; 35=Bandwidth Request Event(optional); 36=Doorbell Event(optional,virtualization only); 37=Host Controller Event; 38=Device Notification Event; 39=MFINDEX Wrap Event; 40-47=Reserved; 48-63=Vendor Defined(optional on any ring). Enforcement rule explicitly stated: a TRB type found on a ring where it isn't 'Allowed' per this table generates an error completion -- Command Ring violation -> Command Completion Event with Completion Code=TRB Error; Transfer Ring violation -> Transfer Event with Completion Code=TRB Error; both carry the address of the offending TRB. This is a directly checkable DUT-conformance rule for an xHCI-model scoreboard (illegal-TRB-type-injection negative test).
